key_insight: AI-assisted screening of discharge summaries surfaced potential treatment injuries for clinician review, with 43.0% of flagged signals confirmed as iatrogenic harm.
clinical_relevance: The workflow supported treatment-injury review and led to seven ACC claims, requiring approximately 25–30 minutes of clinician time per week.
method: Six-month, single-site service-evaluation pilot at Wairarapa Hospital, New Zealand.
A large language model screened 2,642 inpatient discharge summaries for potential treatment injury.
Clinicians reviewed all flagged signals and determined whether escalation was appropriate.
evidence_signal: Of 237 candidate signals, clinicians classified 102 as confirmed harm, 43 as possible harm, 81 as no harm and 11 as unsupported outputs.
watch_item: Without an independent chart-review reference standard, this single-site pilot cannot establish sensitivity or how many injuries screening missed.
paper_title: AI-assisted identification of potential treatment injury from inpatient discharge summaries: an early-stage sociotechnical evaluation in a New Zealand district hospital
